text:
Hi, I’m Tobias Reyne — a full stack developer with 7 years of experience building polished web products with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, and Tailwind CSS.

I’d be excited to help build your Print on Demand Shopify store for beachsoulclothing.cm. Your brand direction sounds strong, and I like that you’re looking for someone who can not only execute the store build, but also bring creative input to improve the product presentation and overall shopping experience. I can help you structure the store for a clean, compelling launch and organize the phase-one catalog of 50 to 60 items in a way that feels cohesive and easy to browse.

While my background is in full stack product development rather than visual design alone, I’m comfortable working closely with provided design direction and translating it into a functional, well-structured storefront. I pay attention to layout, user flow, responsiveness, and conversion-friendly details so the store feels professional across desktop and mobile. I can also support Shopify-related implementation needs and help make sure the product pages and collection structure are set up clearly for a growing catalog.

One project I’m proud of is Embedded customer analytics for a confidential B2B SaaS client. I built usage dashboards embedded directly inside the product so each customer account could see its own metrics. The rollout reached 140 customer accounts, and I delivered it 3 weeks early. That project required careful front-end implementation, reliable data handling, and a focus on a smooth end-user experience — all of which carry over well to ecommerce work where presentation and usability matter.

For your project, I’d be happy to collaborate on the initial store build, product organization, and any technical pieces needed to support a strong launch. If helpful, I can also work on a milestone-based plan so we can move from setup to catalog population to final polish in a structured way.

I can share two relevant samples of work upon request, and I’d be glad to discuss whether an hourly rate or project price makes the most sense for your timeline.
